why: Each position of the output is a choice among the values not yet used: the standard permutation backtracking with a used set. Choosing values in sorted order makes the output come out lexicographic.
hints: Fill the first slot, then the second from what is left. What do you need to remember about which values are already placed?
Sort nums, then DFS: at each depth try every unused value in ascending order, mark it used, recurse, unmark. Visiting in ascending order yields lexicographic output automatically.
Path list + used boolean array; record a copy when the path has n values. O(n * n!) time.
pitfalls: Append a copy of the path, not the path itself, or every row ends up as the same (emptied) list.
The input is not necessarily sorted; sort first to get lexicographic order.
